citation: Wasserthal J, Breit HC, Meyer MT, Pradella M, Hinck D, Sauter AW, Heye T, Boll DT, Cyriac J, Yang S, Bach M, Segeroth M. TotalSegmentator: robust segmentation of 104 anatomic structures in CT images. Radiology: Artificial Intelligence 2023;5(5):e230024.
venue_and_status: Radiology: Artificial Intelligence, published (abstract read in PubMed); methods read in the arXiv preprint 2208.05868
problem: A ready-to-use, robust segmenter for all major anatomic structures in body CT.
method: nnU-Net trained at 1.5 mm (plus a 3 mm fast model) with an iterative model-assisted annotation workflow.
data: 1204 routine CT examinations (2012, 2016, 2020): 1082 training, 57 validation, remainder test; 104 structures; ageing study on 4004 CTs.
main_result: Dice 0.943 (95% CI 0.938-0.947) on the test set; Dice 0.932 vs 0.871 against a BTCV-trained nnU-Net on a separate dataset.
relevance: Most widely used open CT segmenter; the published description refers to version 1 (README), while v2 and later are retrained releases (see T5-P02).
not_established: No measurement agreement across versions, no longitudinal change, no lesions.

citation: Wasserthal J and contributors. TotalSegmentator software documentation: README.md, resources/improvements_in_v2.md, CHANGELOG.md, release and weights tags v1.0-v3.0.0, issues #179 and #445 (GitHub, wasserth/TotalSegmentator); PyPI release history. Accessed 12 October 2026.
venue_and_status: Software documentation and developer statements; not peer reviewed; moving target (accessed 2026-10-12)
problem: Document what changed between releases of a deployed CT segmenter.
method: Developer release notes, weights tags, PyPI history and issue threads, read in full.
data: 36 PyPI releases from 1.0 (2022-08-04) to 2.18.0 (2026-08-12); 39 software tags and 8 weights tags to v3.0.0 (2026-09-07).
main_result: v1 to v2: all models retrained, training images increased from 1139 to 1559, systematic label errors corrected (e.g. liver, spleen, kidney, aorta), class order changed and heart chambers moved to a subtask; 'The resulting segmentations will also be slightly different from v1, because all models have been retrained.' Developer (issue #179): 'the methods are just identical to v1. We just added more data and classes.' Minor releases changed inference and post-processing: step size 0.5 to 0.8 (2.1.0), rib-label-order bug fix (2.2.1), MR models retrained with double data 'results can be different' (2.5.0), resampling bug fixes (2.8.0, 2.9.0), heart-chamber post-processing (2.12.0), coronary and lung-vessel models replaced with LEGACY versions kept (2.13.0), default resampling order 3 to 1 (2.16.0); --report run manifest records software and model versions (2.15.0). v3.0.0 weights asset names indicate 1830 subjects for organs, cardiac and muscle parts. Issue #445: two runs of v1.5.6 on the same series need not give identical masks ('variability is minimal').
relevance: A real release history of exactly the update type the manuscript simulates (retraining on more data with fixed method), together with the preprocessing, threshold and post-processing changes its limitations name.
not_established: No quantitative comparison of volumes between versions; developer statements are not peer reviewed; v3 subject counts inferred from file names.
code_or_data: Open source (Apache-2.0 code; some tasks non-commercial)

citation: Akinci D'Antonoli T, Berger LK, Indrakanti AK, Vishwanathan N, Weiss J, Jung M, Berkarda Z, Rau A, Reisert M, Küstner T, Walter A, Merkle EM, Boll DT, Breit HC, Nicoli AP, Segeroth M, Cyriac J, Yang S, Wasserthal J. TotalSegmentator MRI: robust sequence-independent segmentation of multiple anatomic structures in MRI. Radiology 2025;314(2):e241613.
venue_and_status: Radiology, published
problem: Extend TotalSegmentator to MRI of any sequence.
method: nnU-Net trained on MRI and CT for 80 structures; compared with two public models and TotalSegmentator CT.
data: 1143 scans (616 MRI, 527 CT): 1088 training, 55 internal MRI test; AMOS and CHAOS external sets; 8672 MRIs for an ageing study.
main_result: Dice 0.839 internally; 0.862 vs 0.759 and 0.838 vs 0.560 against other models; 0.966 vs 0.970 against TotalSegmentator CT on 89 CTs.
relevance: Shows the TotalSegmentator family growing across modalities and releases; its MR models were later retrained with about twice the subjects (CHANGELOG 2.5.0: 'results can be different from previous versions').
not_established: No cross-version agreement; no longitudinal or lesion analysis.

citation: Hinck D, Segeroth M, Miazza J, Berdajs D, Bremerich J, Wasserthal J, Pradella M. Automatic segmentation of cardiovascular structures on chest CT data sets: an update of the TotalSegmentator. European Journal of Radiology 2025;185:112006.
venue_and_status: European Journal of Radiology, published
problem: Add and enhance cardiovascular structures in TotalSegmentator.
method: Retraining on an expanded TotalSegmentator dataset; 11 structures added and 6 enhanced; Dice and NSD with Mann-Whitney tests against the previous structures.
data: 1613 CTs (1472 training, 57 validation, 84 test); external Dongyang dataset.
main_result: Median Dice 0.967 and NSD 1.000; Dice and NSD significantly increased for 5 of 6 previously included structures; external Dice 0.970.
relevance: A peer-reviewed update of a deployed CT segmenter, evaluated with overlap metrics only.
not_established: No measurement of the volume shift between old and updated model.

citation: Ma J, He Y, Li F, Han L, You C, Wang B. Segment anything in medical images. Nature Communications 2024;15:654.
venue_and_status: Nature Communications, published (full text via Europe PMC)
problem: A universal promptable segmentation foundation model for medical images.
method: SAM ViT-B fine-tuned with bounding-box prompts simulated from expert masks with a random 0-20 pixel perturbation; 3D images processed slice by slice.
data: 1,570,263 image-mask pairs across 10 modalities; 86 internal and 60 external validation tasks; adrenal tumour annotation-time study.
main_result: Outperformed SAM and matched or exceeded modality-specific U-Net and DeepLabV3+ models (authors' summary).
relevance: Canonical promptable model: the output depends on the user's box. Lineage MedSAM to LiteMedSAM (released 2024-01-15) to MedSAM2 (2025-04-07) per the repository.
not_established: No volumetric reproducibility across prompts, users or releases.

citation: Ma J, Yang Z, Kim S, Chen B, Baharoon M, Fallahpour A, Asakereh R, Lyu H, Wang B. MedSAM2: segment anything in 3D medical images and videos. arXiv:2504.03600, 2025.
venue_and_status: arXiv preprint v1; no published version found on 2026-10-12
problem: Promptable 3D image and video segmentation.
method: SAM2 fine-tuned on a large medical dataset; human-in-the-loop annotation pipeline.
data: Over 455,000 3D image-mask pairs and 76,000 frames; user study annotating 5,000 CT lesions, 3,984 liver MRI lesions and 251,550 echocardiogram frames.
main_result: Outperformed previous models; reduced manual annotation cost by more than 85% (authors).
relevance: Successor release of MedSAM; illustrates that promptable models are re-released with new weights and architectures.
not_established: No volumetric consistency with MedSAM or across prompts; preprint.

citation: Wang H, Guo S, Ye J, Deng Z, Cheng J, Li T, Chen J, Su Y, Huang Z, Shen Y, Fu B, Zhang S, He J. SAM-Med3D: a vision foundation model for general-purpose segmentation on volumetric medical images. IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems 2025;36(10):17599-17612.
venue_and_status: IEEE TNNLS, published (not read); earlier ECCV 2024 Workshops chapter (LNCS, pp. 51-67) and arXiv 2310.15161 v3 (abstract read)
problem: General-purpose promptable 3D segmentation.
method: Fully 3D SAM-style model prompted with 3D points; two-stage training.
data: SA-Med3D-140K: 22K 3D images and 143K masks; evaluation on 16 datasets.
main_result: Accurate segmentation of diverse structures from a few point prompts (authors). README: SAM-Med3D-turbo, fine-tuned on 44 datasets, released later and recommended.
relevance: Promptable 3D model with successive checkpoints (base, turbo).
not_established: No measurement consistency across checkpoints or prompts.

citation: He Y, Guo P, Tang Y, Myronenko A, Nath V, Xu Z, Yang D, Zhao C, Simon B, Belue M, Harmon S, Turkbey B, Xu D, Li W. VISTA3D: a unified segmentation foundation model for 3D medical imaging. In: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR); 2025. p. 20863-20873.
venue_and_status: CVPR 2025, published (not read); arXiv 2406.05285 v3 abstract read
problem: One 3D CT model for automatic, interactive and zero-shot segmentation.
method: 3D model with 127-class automatic segmentation, point-click interactive correction and supervoxel-based zero-shot segmentation.
data: Large and diverse 3D CT benchmarks (details not read).
main_result: State-of-the-art automatic and interactive 3D segmentation (authors). MONAI bundle versions 0.4.1 to 0.5.13 include inference changes ('use 0.3 overlap for inference' in 0.4.8; 'change sw padding mode to replicate' in 0.5.7).
relevance: Deployable CT foundation model distributed as versioned MONAI bundles.
not_established: No measurement agreement across bundle versions or prompts.

citation: Isensee F, Rokuss M, Krämer L, Dinkelacker S, Ravindran A, Stritzke F, Hamm B, Wald T, Langenberg M, Ulrich C, Deissler J, Floca R, Maier-Hein K. nnInteractive: redefining 3D promptable segmentation. arXiv:2503.08373, 2025.
venue_and_status: arXiv preprint v1; no published version found on 2026-10-12
problem: Open-set interactive 3D segmentation integrated in clinical viewers.
method: 3D promptable model accepting points, scribbles, boxes and lasso prompts; 2D interactions produce 3D masks.
data: Trained on 120+ volumetric datasets (CT, MRI, PET, 3D microscopy).
main_result: Far surpasses existing methods (authors); README: first place in the CVPR 2025 interactive 3D challenge.
relevance: Likely deployed promptable model. README: checkpoint nnInteractive_v1.0; software 1.1.0 to 2.5.0 (Aug 2025 to Jun 2026) changed inference (blocky-prediction bug fix 1.1.0; refinement covers the whole mask 1.1.4; half-precision interactions only and GPU preprocessing 2.0.0); the default model id tracks the 'recommended' model unless pinned.
not_established: No volumetric reproducibility analysis; effect of software releases on outputs not documented; preprint.
code_or_data: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnInteractive (Apache-2.0); weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 on Hugging Face

citation: Zhao T, Gu Y, Yang J, Usuyama N, Lee HH, Kiblawi S, Naumann T, Gao J, Crabtree A, Abel J, Moung-Wen C, Piening B, Bifulco C, Wei M, Poon H, Wang S. A foundation model for joint segmentation, detection and recognition of biomedical objects across nine modalities. Nature Methods 2025;22(1):166-176.
venue_and_status: Nature Methods, published (not read); arXiv 2405.12971 v3 abstract read
problem: Text-prompted joint segmentation, detection and recognition.
method: BiomedParse trained jointly on image-mask-text triples harmonized with GPT-4.
data: Over six million triples; 82 object types; 9 modalities; 102,855 test triples.
main_result: Outperformed state-of-the-art methods on segmentation and detection (authors). README: v2 uses the BoltzFormer architecture, release complete 15 Oct 2025; 'use the released v2 weights for 3D modalities and v1 for the rest'; 'We recommend using the latest version of the model.'
relevance: A foundation model whose update changed the architecture, with the developers recommending the newest version.
not_established: No comparison of measurements between v1 and v2.

citation: Pai S, Hadzic I, Bontempi D, Bressem K, Kann BH, Fedorov A, Mak RH, Aerts HJWL. Vision foundation models for computed tomography. arXiv:2501.09001, 2025.
venue_and_status: arXiv preprint v2; no published version found on 2026-10-12
problem: A large pre-trained 3D CT foundation model.
method: Label-agnostic contrastive pre-training (CT-FM), then task adaptation.
data: 148,000 CT scans from the Imaging Data Commons; whole-body and tumour segmentation, head CT triage, retrieval, semantic tasks.
main_result: Superior performance against state-of-the-art models; robust across test-retest settings (authors; embedding level).
relevance: Representative CT foundation backbone from which segmenters are fine-tuned.
not_established: No volumetric consistency of downstream segmentations; preprint.

citation: de Grauw MJJ, Scholten ETh, Smit EJ, Rutten MJCM, Prokop M, van Ginneken B, Hering A. The ULS23 challenge: a baseline model and benchmark dataset for 3D universal lesion segmentation in computed tomography. Medical Image Analysis 2025;102:103525.
venue_and_status: Medical Image Analysis, published (not read); full text read in arXiv 2406.05231 v2
problem: Click-guided 3D universal lesion segmentation in CT.
method: Challenge with VOIs centred on a simulated click; Dice, long- and short-axis SMAPE, and a segmentation consistency score comparing re-aligned outputs for the same lesion prompted at different clicks; nnU-Net baselines.
data: Test set of 725 lesions from 284 patients at two Dutch centres; compiled public and new training data.
main_result: Baseline (nnU-Net ResEnc, semi-supervised): Dice 0.703 +/- 0.240, long-axis SMAPE 11.2%, short-axis 12.0%, consistency Dice 0.787 +/- 0.252. Test Dice 0.651 for default nnU-Net vs 0.700 for the residual-encoder variant. Authors: changing the click location changes the prediction ('intra-observer variability' of the model).
relevance: Quantifies prompt-location sensitivity of a CT lesion segmenter and the size of an architecture-configuration change.
not_established: Consistency measured as Dice, not volume; no longitudinal or version analysis; single reader.

citation: Machado L, Alberge L, Philippe H, Ferreres E, Khlaut J, Dupuis J, Le Floch K, Habip Gatenyo D, Roux P, Grégory J, Ronot M, Dancette C, Boeken T, Tordjman D, Manceron P, Hérent P. A promptable CT foundation model for solid tumor evaluation. npj Precision Oncology 2025;9:121.
venue_and_status: npj Precision Oncology, published (full text via Europe PMC)
problem: Interactive 3D tumour segmentation for RECIST and volumetry.
method: ONCOPILOT: SAM-initialized, pre-trained on anatomy (ONCOPILOT-zero) then fine-tuned on tumours; point, box and point-edit (4 edits) prompts; slice-wise propagation.
data: More than 8000 CTs; ULS23/DeepLesion held-out test; external multicentric longitudinal cohort; three radiologists.
main_result: Test Dice 0.70 (point), 0.70 (box), 0.79 (point-edit) vs 0.70 for the ULS23 baseline; external 0.68, 0.70, 0.79 vs 0.66; ONCOPILOT-zero 0.58 and SAM-Med3D-turbo 0.44. Long-axis median error 14.1% (point) vs 9.6% (point-edit). Inter-reader deviation 1.7 vs 2.4 mm with vs without assistance.
relevance: A company's promptable CT tumour model: prompt mode and model version (pre-trained vs fine-tuned) change accuracy.
not_established: No volumetric reproducibility across prompts or versions; no change error; company-affiliated authors.

citation: Abel L, Wasserthal J, Meyer MT, Vosshenrich J, Yang S, Donners R, Obmann M, Boll D, Merkle E, Breit HC, Segeroth M. Intra-individual reproducibility of automated abdominal organ segmentation: performance of TotalSegmentator compared to human readers and an independent nnU-Net model. Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine 2025;38(3):1617-1627.
venue_and_status: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine, published (online 2024; full text via Europe PMC)
problem: Reproducibility of TotalSegmentator organ volumes across contrast phases.
method: TotalSegmentator vs two readers and an nnU-Net trained on 30 BTCV CTs; relative and absolute volume deviation (AVD); non-inferiority with a 5% margin.
data: 1252 triphasic abdominal CTs (3756 series), 34 structures, 2012-2022.
main_result: 29 of 34 structures within 5%; AVD 6.50% (6.41-6.59) for TotalSegmentator vs 10.03% (9.86-10.20) for the BTCV nnU-Net; in fluid cases 7.93% vs 16.21%.
relevance: Same framework (nnU-Net), different training data: the measurement's reproducibility changed, a training-data effect on measurement behaviour.
not_established: TotalSegmentator version not stated; no between-model or between-version agreement; no lesions or longitudinal change.

citation: Auriac J, Nioche C, Hovhannisyan-Baghdasarian N, Loisel C, Seban RD, Jehanno N, Sundar LKS, Beyer T, Buvat I, Orlhac F. Comparison of organ volumes and standardized uptake values in [18F]FDG-PET/CT images using MOOSE and TotalSegmentator to segment CT images. Medical Physics 2025;52(10):e70025.
venue_and_status: Medical Physics, published (full text via Europe PMC)
problem: Are two whole-body CT segmenters interchangeable for volumes and SUV?
method: MOOSE v3.0.14 and TotalSegmentator v2.0.5 (both nnU-Net based); relative difference per VOI.
data: 315 women with metastatic breast cancer, baseline FDG PET/CT; 33 VOIs.
main_result: Volumes differed by less than 10% for 19/33 organs in at least 80% of patients; adrenal glands, bladder, portal/splenic veins and thyroid differed by 20% or more in at least 20% of patients; volumes differed significantly for 28/33 structures; largest differences bladder 48%, veins 34%, thyroid 16%, adrenals 15%; MOOSE excluded pleural effusion and some metastases.
relevance: Size of the volume shift from swapping between two tools of the same architecture family but different training data and label conventions.
not_established: No lesion volumes, no longitudinal change, no version-to-version comparison; female cohort only.

citation: Giebeler L, Krishnaswamy D, Clunie DA, Wasserthal J, Sundar LKS, Diaz-Pinto A, Maier-Hein KH, Xu M, Menze BH, Pieper SD, Kikinis R, Fedorov A. In search of truth: evaluating concordance of AI-based anatomy segmentation models. Journal of Medical Imaging 2026;13(6):062204.
venue_and_status: Journal of Medical Imaging, published (not read); full text read in arXiv 2512.15921 v2, which links the published version
problem: Compare segmentation models without ground truth.
method: Harmonized DICOM SEG; consensus (voxels segmented by all models) DSC and consensus-to-model volume ratio; visual review.
data: Six models (TotalSegmentator 1.5 and 2.6, Auto3DSeg, MOOSE 3.0, MultiTalent, CADS); 18 CT series from 4 NLST patients; 24 structures.
main_result: Lungs DSC above 95% and volume agreement above 90%; TotalSegmentator 1.5 segments heart substructures whereas 2.6 has a single heart label; heart consensus volume 60-85% of model volumes (4 models); ribs 45-90%; vertebrae 0-95% with errors in the four TotalSegmentator-dataset models.
relevance: Model swaps, including a TotalSegmentator version change, alter structure definitions and volumes.
not_established: Four patients, no ground truth, descriptive; no lesions or longitudinal measurement.

citation: Kobayashi R, Sekine T, Imai S, Sohara K, Ando T, Tanaka A, Yan N, Hayashi H, Kumita SI. Technical feasibility of AI-based longitudinal multi-organ volumetry on low-dose PET/CT over 13 years. Japanese Journal of Radiology 2026 (online 23 September 2026).
venue_and_status: Japanese Journal of Radiology, published online ahead of print
problem: Longitudinal stability of TotalSegmentator volumetry on low-dose CT.
method: Fast vs Normal inference modes and five denoising methods compared by detrended within-participant CV; linear mixed-effects trends.
data: Screening registry: 10 participants (137 scans) for pipeline choice; 30 participants aged 60+ (337 scans) over about 13 years.
main_result: Fast mode similar detrended variability to Normal (CV 2.26-9.32% across six structures), about 10-fold faster; denoising did not help; e.g. liver -0.55%/year.
relevance: Closest inspected study of the longitudinal consistency of a public CT segmenter's volumetry; one pipeline per participant.
not_established: No mixing of modes or versions within a participant; software version not given in the abstract.

citation: Suri A, Mukherjee P, Rabbee N, Pickhardt PJ, Summers RM. Assessing the reliability of pancreatic CT imaging biomarkers for diabetes prediction: a dual center retrospective study. Academic Radiology 2025;32(7):4013-4021.
venue_and_status: Academic Radiology, published (author manuscript read via PMC)
problem: Robustness of pancreatic CT biomarkers to the segmentation algorithm.
method: TotalSegmentator, nnU-Net (MSD Task07) and DM-UNet; ICC (two-way random, single measures) across algorithms; diabetes prediction models.
data: 9772 patients at two institutions.
main_result: Attenuation biomarkers ICC 0.93 or more; pancreatic volume ICC 0.50 (0.48-0.51) overall, 0.55 non-contrast, 0.37 contrast; 3D fractal dimension 0.15; prediction AUC 0.84-0.91.
relevance: Large-sample evidence that replacing the segmenter changes organ volume much more than attenuation.
not_established: No tumour volumes, versions or longitudinal change.

citation: Chattopadhyay S, Demir B, Niethammer M. On the robustness of foundational 3D medical image segmentation models against imprecise visual prompts. arXiv:2601.16383, 2026 (accepted at ISBI 2026 per the arXiv comment).
venue_and_status: arXiv preprint v1; ISBI 2026 acceptance stated by authors, proceedings version not checked
problem: Robustness of 3D promptable models to imprecise dense prompts.
method: Controlled dilation and erosion (radius 1-8 voxels), boundary-preserving erosion and spatial shifts of mask prompts for SAM-Med3D and nnInteractive; Dice.
data: BTCV multi-organ abdominal CT.
main_result: Performance falls with prompt coarseness; nnInteractive follows dilated or eroded mask prompts and segments beyond true boundaries; small or irregular organs suffer more from shifts; SAM-Med3D robust to shifts for most organs.
relevance: Outputs, and so volumes, follow an imprecise mask prompt: relevant where an earlier mask is propagated as the follow-up prompt.
not_established: No volumes in mL, lesions or longitudinal data.

citation: Julius Blöcker T, Delopoulos N, Palacios MA, Klüter S, Hörner-Rieber J, Rippke C, Placidi L, Boldrini L, Frascino V, Andratschke N, Baumgartl M, Dal Bello R, Marschner SN, Belka C, Corradini S, Dudas D, Riboldi M, Kurz C, Landry G. GTV segmentation in MRI guided radiotherapy with promptable foundation models. Physics in Medicine & Biology 2026;71(1):015006.
venue_and_status: Physics in Medicine & Biology, published online 29 Dec 2025 (CC BY 4.0; full text blocked by publisher captcha)
problem: Promptable foundation models for GTV delineation on MRI-linac images.
method: SAM2, MedSAM2 and nnInteractive prompted with six sparse prompt types (points, boxes, 2D masks); DSC and other metrics.
data: Multi-institutional clinical GTVs (abdomen, lung, liver, pancreas, pelvis) on MRI-linac scans.
main_result: Median DSC up to 0.85 (nnInteractive, mask prompt); median DSC over all prompt types 0.75 nnInteractive, 0.70 MedSAM2, 0.54 SAM2; prompts with more spatial information gave better results with lower variance, an effect reduced for nnInteractive and MedSAM2.
relevance: Same-venue evidence that the segmentation depends on both the model and the prompt.
not_established: No volume metrics; MRI; no longitudinal or version analysis.

citation: Baldeon-Calisto M, Perez-Pérez N, Guevara C. Is segmentation solved? An evaluation of vision foundation models for head and neck tumor segmentation. Physics in Medicine & Biology 2026;71(10):105026.
venue_and_status: Physics in Medicine & Biology, published
problem: Zero- and few-shot foundation models for head and neck tumour segmentation.
method: SAM, MedSAM and nnInteractive with boxes enlarged up to twice the tight box; UniverSeg and SegGPT with growing support sets; two-factor repeated-measures ANOVA.
data: Head and neck cancer GTVp and GTVn (dataset details not read).
main_result: Model and prompting strategy both had significant effects; larger boxes notably degraded SAM, MedSAM and nnInteractive; supervised CNNs were more stable and clinically reliable.
relevance: Same-venue evidence that architecture and prompt both change the output.
not_established: No volume metrics; no longitudinal or version analysis.

citation: Wang Y, Shi V, Hsu WC, Dai Y, Yao S, Zhong Z, Zhang Z, Wu J, Maxwell A, Collins S, Jiao Z, Bai HX. Optimizing prompt strategies for SAM: advancing lesion segmentation across diverse medical imaging modalities. Physics in Medicine & Biology 2025;70(17):175014.
venue_and_status: Physics in Medicine & Biology, published
problem: Effect of SAM prompt number and placement on lesion segmentation.
method: Manual vs SAM-assisted segmentation; reinforcement-learning agent for prompt placement; pairwise t-tests.
data: Four lesion datasets (ovarian, lung, renal and breast tumours).
main_result: Ovarian tumour Dice 0.272 with one point vs 0.806 with five or more; surface and union prompts outperformed centre prompts (mean Dice 0.604 ovarian, 0.724 breast).
relevance: Magnitude of prompt dependence for lesions.
not_established: Dice only; no volumes or longitudinal analysis.

citation: Wuts J, Ceranka J, Giordano L, Michoux N, Pasoglou V, Vandemeulebroucke J, Lecouvet F. Benchmarking lesion-level response assessment of metastatic bone disease on WB-MRI using manual, interactive and automated segmentation methods. In: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI); 2026. p. 1-4.
venue_and_status: ISBI 2026 proceedings, published
problem: Are lesion measurements precise enough for response decision bands?
method: Manual RECIST diameters vs nnInteractive semi-automated segmentation vs a fully automated model; agreement, reproducibility and decision-band detectability (20% RECIST, 66% volumetric RECIST, 25% ADC).
data: 40 advanced prostate cancer patients, skeletal metastases on whole-body MRI.
main_result: Interactive segmentation had the highest agreement with reference and excellent reliability for volume; the automated model did not yield reliable response assessment; experts rated interactive masks equal or better than manual ground truth for 83% of lesions.
relevance: Volumetric reproducibility of a promptable model judged against response thresholds.
not_established: MRI; reproducibility numbers not in the abstract; no version analysis.

citation: Gesierich B, Pirpamer L, Meier DS, Amann M, Cerfontaine MN, de Leeuw FE, Maillard P, Moy S, Helmer KG, Kühne M, Bonati LH, Rutten JW, Lesnik Oberstein SAJ, Duering M. Technical and clinical validation of a novel deep learning-based white matter hyperintensity segmentation tool. Cerebral Circulation - Cognition and Behavior 2025;9:100393.
venue_and_status: Cerebral Circulation - Cognition and Behavior, published (full text via Europe PMC)
problem: Validate a WMH volume biomarker tool.
method: MD-GRU and nnU-Net trained on the same 277 heterogeneous scans; Bland-Altman bias and limits of agreement vs STAPLE reference; scan-rescan and inter-scanner reproducibility; power to detect a 30% effect on 2-year volume change.
data: MarkVCID (42 scan-rescan, 20 inter-scanner patients), Swiss-AF 2D data (55), DiViNAS CADASIL cohort (126, 2-year follow-up).
main_result: Constant bias -1.07 vs -0.86 and one-sided LOA 2.33 vs 1.88 (MD-GRU vs nnU-Net; untransformed WMH volume, units not stated in the extracted text); scan-rescan LOA 1.44 vs 1.13; positive 2-year change in 88% vs 92% of patients; sample size per arm 198 vs 161 (benchmarks 274 and 311).
relevance: Architecture change with the training data held fixed: similar cross-sectional agreement but different longitudinal sensitivity.
not_established: Each architecture measured both timepoints (no mixing); brain MRI; reference built from the algorithms' consensus.

citation: Mehta PM, Yayli SB, Rai P, Sonka M, Blezek DJ, Zhang H, Silvera VM, Benson JC, Carlson ML, Erickson BJ, Bathla G. Comparative evaluation of deep learning models for 3D segmentation and volumetry of vestibular schwannomas using large heterogeneous data sets with external validation. AJNR American Journal of Neuroradiology 2026;47(5):1266-1272.
venue_and_status: AJNR, published
problem: Which architecture to use for tumour volumetry on serial MRI.
method: nnU-Net (Base, ResEncL), U-Mamba, UNETR and MedSAM trained on the same data; Dice, Hausdorff, surface distance, relative volume error (RVE).
data: 2692 training scans (383 patients); internal test 277 scans (97 patients); external public test set of 241.
main_result: External median Dice 0.899-0.927 (U-Mamba highest, then nnU-Net Base and ResEncL); for the top three, median RVE 0.07-0.08 as reported in the abstract (units ambiguous).
relevance: Same-data architecture comparison that includes a volume error.
not_established: No between-architecture per-lesion volume differences; no longitudinal change; MedSAM and UNETR volume results not in the abstract.

citation: Zhao L, Luo Y, Mok V, Shi L. Automated brain volumetric measures with AccuBrain: version comparison in accuracy, reproducibility and application for diagnosis. BMC Medical Imaging 2022;22:117.
venue_and_status: BMC Medical Imaging, published (full text via Europe PMC)
problem: Compare two versions of a commercial brain volumetry tool after a segmentation-algorithm update.
method: AccuBrain IV1.2 vs IV2.0 on public datasets: hippocampal DSC vs manual, AD-RAI diagnostic AUC, intra-scanner ICC.
data: ADNI, EADC-ADNI, MIRIAD (short-interval rescans).
main_result: IV2.0 DSC 0.910 vs 0.892 (left) and 0.912 vs 0.890 (right); AUC 0.977 vs 0.921; reproducibility similar; 'both versions should be feasible for use'.
